Kyrgios, who had been ​provisionally suspended since August 4, had ‌entered into a treatment programme approved by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) to ​reduce the three-month default suspension under WADA rules. The Australian gave a sample at an ATP tournament in Majorca in June which tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine. messages.text: Inside the neighbourhood club that made Arteta, Alonso and Iraola

metadata.summary: Between a row of white apartment buildings and an artificial pitch set into the green hills of Berio in San Sebastian that Antiguoko now call home, there is a strip of land where Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola learned their craft.
metadata.content: Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola started their paths to the top at Antiguoko: 'If I really think about it, it's absolutely crazy' | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola started their paths to the top at Antiguoko: 'If I really think about it, it's absolutely crazy' Born within 15 miles of each other and only seven months apart, the managers of Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool are all products of Antiguoko; Sky Sports visited the tiny Basque club to hear how it all began for Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola Nick Wright Football Features Writer @nicholaspwright Thursday 3 September 2026 21:43, UK Image: Xabi Alonso, Mikel Arteta and Andoni Iraola are products of Antiguoko Between a row of white apartment buildings and an artificial pitch set into the green hills of Berio in San Sebastian that Antiguoko now call home, there is a strip of land where Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola learned their craft. "The centre circle was just over there," says Roberto Montiel, the club's long-serving coach and vice-president, as he takes a seat in what is now a public park. He rubs his thumb and forefinger together as he recalls the texture of the old playing surface. "The pitch wasn't like the new one up there. It was smaller and made of small stones, like gravel. messages.text: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching 'smear campaign' against Infantino

metadata.summary: FIFA has accused European football’s governing body of launching a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino in a challenge to legal action over the aborted attempt to sell part of the World Cup to private investors.
metadata.content: Gianni Infantino latest: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching a 'smear campaign' after legal cases filed in American courts | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Gianni Infantino latest: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching a 'smear campaign' after legal cases filed in American courts UEFA has warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland, where FIFA has its headquarters, and has filed legal cases in American courts. Rob Harris Sports correspondent, Sky News Friday 4 September 2026 07:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player UEFA has warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Gianni Infantino in Switzerland, where FIFA has its headquarters, and has filed legal cases in American courts. FIFA has accused European football’s governing body of launching a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino in a challenge to legal action over the aborted attempt to sell part of the World Cup to private investors. UEFA has filed legal cases in American courts seeking evidence relating to the controversial venture and warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland where FIFA has its headquarters. FIFA has now filed a response in a New York court, saying: "While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership." But the seamer was rewarded for simplicity on Thursday as a five-wicket haul - her first in international cricket - helped her side wrap up an one-day international series win over Ireland. Prioritising the wobble-seam delivery that angled in to the right handers, Wong bowled opposition captain Gaby Lewis through the gate for her first strike of the day.
